summary.text: A 78-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension, coronary artery disease with prior myocardial infarction requiring stent placement, asthma, gastroesophageal reflux disease and bulbar poliomyelitis presented to a Primary Care clinic with worsening fatigue, exertional shortness of breath, dysphagia, chest tightness and generalized weakness. He reported poliomyelitis diagnosed in 1956, complicated by dysphagia requiring tracheostomy placement, with appropriate recovery and few noticeable sequelae.

Vital signs and routine blood testing were normal and examination showed mild bilateral upper extremity weakness with otherwise intact neurological and normal remaining examinations. Outpatient workup found right hemidiaphragm eventration and elevation on high resolution CT, very mild restriction with total lung capacity 79%, mild obstructive sleep apnea, sinus rhythm, ejection fraction 70% with an unchanged non-reversible infarction, and a hiatal hernia with a Schatzki ring requiring balloon dilation on EGD.

Post-polio syndrome was diagnosed given the distant history of poliomyelitis, mostly negative multi-system workup and presenting signs. An Auto-PAP was issued for sleep apnea and physical therapy was recommended with an emphasis on avoiding overexertion.
